title: Learning to Say No
paragraphs: For years, Basma agreed to nearly every request from friends and family, believing that constant availability was simply what being a good, generous person required of her at all times.
This pattern eventually led to genuine exhaustion, and she began resenting the very people she was trying to help, an emotional cost she had not anticipated when she first developed this habit.

A close friend eventually pointed out that Basma's constant yes had actually made her less present and less genuine in the commitments that mattered most, since she was stretched too thin across everything.

Basma began practicing a difficult new skill: politely declining requests that conflicted with her existing priorities, without over-explaining or apologizing excessively for a decision she was entitled to make.
The first few refusals felt uncomfortable, and one relative even seemed briefly offended, but most people, surprisingly, respected her clearer boundaries once she began setting them consistently.
Basma eventually realized that saying no thoughtfully, rather than saying yes automatically, actually allowed her to be more genuinely present and generous in the commitments she chose to keep.
